description: Intercom is a customer messaging and support platform with a REST API, webhooks and an MCP server.
auth_notes: Access Tokens for private apps on your own workspace; OAuth required for public apps accessing other people's data. MCP mentions Bearer tokens tied to a teammate.
gate_detail: OAuth client_id and client_secret come from an app's Basic Information page in the Developer Hub. Sources do not state plan, signup or review requirements for obtaining an Access Token or creating apps.
api_scope: Versioned REST API (2.18) covering admins, articles, companies, contacts, conversations, data attributes, events, help center, messages, news, notes and segments.
mcp_notes: Intercom documents its own MCP server for US and EU workspaces; connection URLs are not shown in the excerpt.
blocker_detail: Sources do not establish what plan or approval is needed to obtain tokens or create a Developer Hub app.

evidence.quote: To access the Intercom API, you have two authentication options depending on whether you app is public or private.
If you are building a public integration that will have access to **other peoples'** Intercom data you are required to set up OAuth.
These can be found on the Basic Information page for your app in the Developer Hub.
Webhook topics are related to corresponding permission scopes
The Intercom MCP server is available for US and EU hosted workspaces.

uncertainties: Access Token creation steps and plan requirements are not in the truncated sources.
Sandbox or test workspace not described.
Whether public OAuth apps need review is not stated.
